title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in July 1986 Grothendieck is axiomatizing an 'atelier' (workshop). This is a set 𝒜 of 'elementary figures' (Figel) in an ambient set or 'space' E. It carries three relations: ⊴ (inclusion-type), ≪̊ (strict or 'interior' inclusion) and |∘| (disjointness or separation). Arbitrary figures ('sommets', the Boolean level) are obtained from elementary ones, with operations Sup, Inf and complement ∁. The previous page built sub-ateliers (strict and broad 'residual ateliers'). This page studies functoriality of ateliers in the underlying set.

(2°) Pullback. A map of sets f: E'→E, or of the structured 'espaces modulés/modelés', gives the preimage map f*: Figures(E)→Figures(E'). An elementary figure can have empty preimage when f is not surjective. So f* sends Figel(E)=𝒜 only into 𝒜'∪{∅}, where ∅ is the 'figure vide'. f* respects ⊴, ≪̊ and |∘| but is not injective in general. On the Boolean level ('passage aux sommets') preimage commutes with all operations: arbitrary Sup, arbitrary Inf and complement.

(3°) Pushforward along an injection. For g: E→E' injective, direct image g_*: 𝒜→𝒜' is injective and respects the three relations. On the Boolean level g_* commutes with:
- arbitrary Sup (unions);
- nonempty Inf (intersections; injectivity is needed here);
- relative complement S∧∁T.
It does not commute with absolute complement, and hence not with the empty Inf (=E), unless g is bijective.

The next page combines 2° and 3° via a correspondence E ←f− Γ −f'→ E' with Γ→E' injective, i.e. pull back then push forward. It notes that there seems to be no direct transfer along a non-injective g: E→E'. For general atelier morphisms one would need 'correspondences'. This is purely a bookkeeping step: establishing which maps of underlying sets induce maps of ateliers, presumably to define a category of ateliers.
errors: 'Compatible with ≪̊' for f* needs a caveat if ≪̊ is a strict relation. When f is not surjective, preimage can identify distinct figures (non-injectivity), so a strict relation may degenerate to equality, or both sides may become ∅. Compatibility holds in the weak sense, or only on pairs with nonempty preimages.
'A tendance à passer aux sommets' is heuristic and not proved here. It depends on the precise definition of sommets in the atelier, which is not on this page.

ideas.what: Preimage of figures along f: E'→E lands in elementary figures plus the empty figure, and commutes with all Boolean operations
ideas.modern_name: Inverse image as a complete Boolean algebra homomorphism P(E)→P(E') (contravariant power-set functor); pointed extension 𝒜'∪{∅}
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard set theory / Boolean algebra (Stone duality folklore)

ideas.what: Direct image along an injection preserves arbitrary unions, nonempty intersections and relative complements, but not complement unless bijective
ideas.modern_name: Direct image along a monomorphism is a frame/lattice embedding onto a principal ideal (a homomorphism of generalized Boolean algebras)

ideas.what: Functoriality of 'ateliers' (sets of elementary figures with relations ⊴, ≪̊, |∘|) along maps of underlying sets, leading to correspondences on the next page
ideas.modern_name: Span/correspondence-based morphisms of incidence structures; closest modern analogues are abstract incidence geometries or simplicial-type combinatorial models of space
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the 1986 reflections on discrete/combinatorial structures of space mentioned around Récoltes et Semailles; unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification of how preimage and injective direct image interact with Boolean operations and the atelier relations. The atelier framework itself is little known, but this page contains nothing beyond standard set-theoretic facts.
transcription_corrections: 'Figel(E) = 𝒜' and 'Figel(E') = 𝒜'': the identifications '=𝒜' and '=𝒜'' are written as superscripts over Figel; the second has a corrected E'.
The rotated marginal note probably reads 'de même dans le cas d'une application d'espaces modulés[/modelés], f* sur figures' (reading uncertain).
The struck-out text before 𝒜'∪{∅} reads 'Figel ∪ {e}' or 'Figel ∪ {∅}'.
The first relation symbol is probably ⊴ (triangle with underbar), consistent with the previous page, rather than ◁.
